author: desk
note: Desk-written plain-English summary, not a tiered fact. Written to help a reader understand the business quickly; verify any figure against the fact store before using it in a report.
one_liner: Generates realistic synthetic speech and voice.
what_it_does: ElevenLabs turns text into speech that sounds human, clones voices with permission, and dubs audio across languages. Customers include publishers, game studios, film and accessibility products.
how_it_makes_money: Subscriptions by volume of audio generated, plus enterprise contracts and a developer interface.
why_it_matters: It is the category leader in a narrow, defensible slice of AI rather than a frontier generalist, which is a different and arguably safer business shape.
competitive_position: Competes with big-cloud speech services and other voice startups. Quality has been its moat, but the gap narrows as general models add audio.
key_risks: Voice cloning invites impersonation and fraud, and regulation is arriving.
General-purpose models are adding good-enough audio for free.
Rights and consent issues around cloned voices carry legal exposure.
A narrow category caps the size of the opportunity.

glossary.definition: Reproducing a specific person's voice from a sample so new speech can be generated in it.
Converting written text into spoken audio.
